newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIAN EXOTICS - Devaluation rumours hit rupiah,baht.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS - Devaluation rumours hit rupiah,baht.

text.p: * Thai baht and Indonesian rupiah hit by devaluation rumours, said started by Singapore players.
* Sharp sell-off in Thai stocks on continuing rumours of defaults at Thai brokerage houses seen triggering further baht sales. Forwards trade choppy.
* Malaysian ringgit and Singapore dollar confined to range trade with lingering fear of central bank intervention capping Sing dollar's rise.
The Thai baht and Indonesian rupiah were hurt by devaluation rumours, apparently started by Singapore players in late morning trade on Friday.

Dealers said there was little obvious rationale behind the rupiah rumours, but Thailand's looming political crisis, the downgrade of short-term currency debt rating by Moody's and market talk of financial defaults at Thai brokerage houses had made the baht very vulnerable.
Desmond Supple, regional economist at consulting firm I.D.E.A. in Singapore told Reuters Financial Television the baht rumour was just the most recent in a stream of periodic devaluation rumours.

"The baht's going to remain susceptible to these given that we are seeing a slowdown in short-term capital inflows to Thailand while at the same time, the current account deficit remains high," Supple said.
Thai stocks continued to be sharply sold on lingering rumours of financial problems at Thai finance and securities houses, despite denials by the firms themselves and by the Bank of Thailand.
Thai stocks fell by 2.27 percent with the index hitting a 35-month low amid forced selling.
A U.S. bank dealer in Singapore said the flight of capital from Thai stocks would keep the baht under pressure.
"People are still suggesting buying the dollar because the corporates in Thailand are doing the same thing, so they might know something we don't," said another Singapore dealer.
The baht weakened to 25.341-25.346 to the dollar at midday from 25.322-25.332 late on Thursday.
In Indonesia, spot rupiah fell to a low of 2,348.75 in early trade. It was quoted at 2,347.25/47.75 at midday against an opening of 2,346.50/47.00.
A Singapore dealer said the rumours of a rupiah devaluation were clearly without basis but gave short-term speculators a chance to capitalise on the situation.
Jakarta dealers said the attack on the rupiah by Singapore players also caused swap rates to edge up but local operators provided some support to the currency.
A U.S. bank dealer in Jakarta said the relatively ample money supply, which kept short-dated swap rates low, also seemed to have created room for speculation on a weakening in the rupiah.
"Some offshore players took the chance to speculate on the rupiah because of the cheap swap rates. They have no problem to finance dollar purchases," the dealer said.
The Malaysian ringgit traded in a tight band but was expected to come under some pressure from overseas investors.
"Nothing much is happening. There is some pressure on ringgit, but I think it will trade in the 2.4960/10 range," said a foreign bank dealer in Kuala Lumpur.
A dealer with a local bank said the U.S. jobs data due at 1230 GMT was not expected to have much impact on the ringgit but investors were not taking chances by keeping their commitments low.
The ringgit was at 2.4990/95 to the dollar against 2.4962/72 at close in Kuala Lumpur on Thursday.
- Madhav Reddy in Kuala Lumpur (603-230 8911), Tang Nguyen in Bangkok (662- 252-9950), Mantik Kusjanto in Jakarta (6221-384-6364) and Sonali Desai in Singapore (65-8703092)
